questions.question: 5 persons A, B, C, D and E are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). A is sitting fourth to the right of C. B is sitting second to the right of C. D is sitting to the immediate left of B. How many persons are sitting to the left of E?
questions.solution:
Logic followed here is the linear arrangement of people in a row facing **North** based on the given directions.

**Step-by-step explanation:**

1) **A is sitting fourth to the right of C:** In a row of 5 persons, this is only possible if **C** is at the 1st position (left end) and **A** is at the 5th position (right end).

2) **B is sitting second to the right of C:** This means **B** occupies the 3rd position from the left (1 + 2 = 3).

3) **D is sitting to the immediate left of B:** Since **B** is at the 3rd position, the position to its immediate left is the 2nd position, which is occupied by **D**.

4) **E is the remaining person:** The only available spot left is the 4th position, which must be occupied by **E**.

**Final Seating Arrangement:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3ef57983d34b66b997ae88538492af29ca6c19bfcbc15b85aeb8ccfe4d11ce8f.png] 

From the final arrangement, we can see that the persons sitting to the left of **E** (at the 4th position) are **C**, **D**, and **B**.

Total number of persons to the left of **E** = 3

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question: Marks of 6 boys A, B, C, D, E and F is compared. Marks of no two boys are same. Marks of C are least. Marks of A are more than only D and C. Marks of B are more than F but less than E. Marks of how many boys are less than E?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

 
• C has the least marks.
 
• A has more marks than only D and C.
 
• B has more marks than F but less than E.
 
• No two boys have the same marks.

**Vertical arrangement:**

 
 

 Rank (Highest → Lowest)

**Explanation:**

Since **C** has the least marks, C is placed at the bottom.

**A** has more marks than only **D** and **C**, so the order is **A > D > C**.

**B** has more marks than **F** but less than **E**, so the order is **E > B > F**.

Combining both groups gives:

**E > B > F > A > D > C**

Boys having less marks than **E** are:

**B, F, A, D, C** = **5 boys**.

**Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1 (5)".**

questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 6 AM and 7 AM will the angle between the hour and the minute hand of a clock be 30 degrees?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The angle between the **hour hand** and the **minute hand** of a clock at any given time can be calculated using the formula:

**Angle (θ) = |30H − (11/2)M|**

Where:

**H** = the value of the hour (between 1 and 12).

**M** = the value of the minutes (between 0 and 59).

__Calculation:__

Given the time is between **6 AM** and **7 AM**, we take **H = 6**.

The required angle between the hands is **30°**.

Substitute these values into the formula:

30 = |30 × 6 − (11/2)M|

30 = |180 − 5.5M|

This equation gives two possible cases:

**Case 1: When the minute hand is behind the hour hand**

180 − 5.5M = 30

5.5M = 180 − 30

5.5M = 150

M = 150/5.5 ≈ **27.27 minutes**

This corresponds to approximately **6:27 AM**.

**Case 2: When the minute hand has crossed the hour hand**

5.5M − 180 = 30

5.5M = 180 + 30

5.5M = 210

M = 210/5.5 = 420/11 ≈ **38.18 minutes**

This corresponds to approximately **6:38 AM**.

Comparing the results with the given options, the time **6:38 AM** is listed as an option.

Hence, the correct answer is **6:38**.

questions.question: A clock shows the correct time at 8 AM. The clock gains 2 seconds every 6 minutes. What time (in PM) will it show at 8 PM the same day?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The time interval from **8 AM** to **8 PM** on the same day is **12 hours**.

Total time in minutes = 12 × 60 = **720 minutes**.

__Calculation:__

Given that the **clock** gains **2 seconds** in every **6 minutes**.

Rate of gain = 2 ÷ 6 = 1/3 **seconds per minute**.

Total gain in 720 minutes = 720 × 1/3 = **240 seconds**.

Converting the total gain into minutes: 240 ÷ 60 = **4 minutes**.

Now, the actual time is **8 PM**.

Time shown by the clock = Actual time + Total gain

Time shown = 8:00:00 + 4 minutes = **8:04:00**.

Hence, the correct answer is **8:04:00**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Clock gain in **1 hour** (60 minutes):

6 minutes = 2 seconds

60 minutes = (2 ÷ 6) × 60 = **20 seconds**.

Total gain in **12 hours** = 12 × 20 = **240 seconds**.

Total gain in minutes = 240 ÷ 60 = **4 minutes**.

Therefore, the time the clock will show at **8 PM** is **8:04:00**.
